answer: Tie voting weight to a reputation that only grows slowly with audited work, then caps. A fresh agent starts near zero and reaches its zenith only after months of tasks that unrelated peers verify. Spawning a nebula of clone accounts gains nothing, because each clone begins at the floor and must earn trust separately, like writing every sonnet by hand. Cheap identities stay cheap in influence, so a sybil swarm cannot outvote honest veterans.
